newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedore reps to decide on national strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedore reps to decide on national strike.

text.p: Delegates of Brazil's National Stevedores' Union will meet at the port of Santos, which began a strike earlier, to decide whether the stoppage should spread nationally.
The representatives from various Brazilian ports will meet at 1400 local/1700 GMT, an official of the union said.

"They will define a fighting plan, some measures, some precautions," he said, adding it was likely the stevedores would call a national port strike for Wednesday. "The way things are now, I think it's likely," he said.
Twenty-two delegates are scheduled to attend the meeting instead of the 30 originally expected because some had difficulty arranging a flight at short notice, the official added.

Workers at Santos began an indefinite strike at 0700 local to protest steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at the port.
The protest paralyzed most loading, with only three out of 20 vessels operating, according to the port authority Codesp.
Military police officers in the early hours removed 26 stevedores who had been occupying two vessels at Cosipa's terminal for the last 13 days.
"They removed them without violence. They went in at 0400 and by 0600 they had already removed all the occupants," said a spokeswoman for the port.

Stevedores were now demonstrating in front of the Cosipa terminal. By 0900, an estimated 500 people were massed in front of the company's terminal but this number could swell as many more were arriving by bus.
Up to 5,000 workers could participate in the protest, Santos Stevedores' Union president Joaquim da Silva said Monday.
"It is very possible because as well as the stevedores, family members are also participating," said the port spokeswoman.

The manifestation was peaceful so far but there was talk it would spread to the motorway leading into the port, which would block the arrival and unloading of trucks which until now was continuing as normal, she said.
